insights.headline: Hawkish Fed and 5%+ yields drive gold's worst weekly stretch since spring
insights.summary: Gold and silver fell for another week as the Fed's September rate hike and signals of more tightening pushed the US 10-year yield above 5.20% and lifted the dollar, overwhelming safe-haven demand from the US-Iran standoff. Spot gold held near $4,270-4,290, down 2-2.4% on the week, while silver fell 3.7-5.3%. On MCX, October gold closed around ₹1.51 lakh per 10 grams, the weaker rupee cushioning the decline. Kotak flagged downside risk to its $88B FY27 gold-import forecast after the May duty hike to 15%, while RBI gold reserves rose as overall forex reserves fell. US jobs data and PCE are next.
points: Spot gold ended near $4,275, down ~2.4% for the week; silver fell 3.7-5.3% as yields above 5% raised the cost of holding bullion.
MCX October gold closed at about ₹1,51,000; a weaker rupee softened the fall for Indian buyers, physical demand stayed selective.
Kotak sees downside to its $88B FY27 gold-import forecast; the 6%-to-15% duty hike and high prices are curbing physical demand.
RBI's gold reserves rose $68M to $111.29B even as total forex reserves fell $14.88B to $765.90B in the week to September 18.
Wall Street is split on next week (36% bullish, 29% bearish, 36% neutral) while 57% of Main Street voters expect gold to rise.

trending.title: Hawkish Fed, 5%+ yields pressure bullion
trending.summary: Sticky inflation and Fed rate-hike bets pushed the 10-year yield above 5.20%, driving gold's fourth weekly loss in five and silver's slide.

trending.title: MCX gold holds near ₹1.51 lakh as rupee cushions fall
trending.summary: Domestic futures tracked global weakness but a softer rupee limited losses; ICICI Bank sees a ₹1.40-1.60 lakh range into year-end.

trending.title: India's gold import demand cools after duty hike
trending.summary: Kotak cut its outlook as the 15% import duty and high prices dent physical buying; NSE is pushing electronic gold receipts instead.

trending.title: Jobs data and PCE to decide gold's next move
trending.summary: With $4,300 support under test, traders await US payrolls and inflation data that could reset Fed rate expectations.

items.title: Gold slides 2% to $4,288, silver falls 3.7% to $63.90 on hawkish Fed, stronger dollar and rising yields
items.summary: Spot gold fell more than 2% for the week to about $4,288 an ounce and silver dropped 3.7% to $63.90 as hawkish Federal Reserve signals, a stronger US dollar and rising Treasury yields pressured bullion. On MCX, October gold closed at ₹1,51,135 per 10 grams while December silver ended at ₹2,33,850 per kg, with the weaker rupee cushioning the domestic decline.

items.title: Gold, silver prices: what is driving volatility in bullion markets
items.summary: MCX October gold rose ₹150 to about ₹1.50 lakh per 10 grams and December silver gained ₹368 to ₹2.33 lakh per kg in Friday trade, though both stayed under weekly pressure from a stronger dollar, US Treasury yields above 5% and higher-for-longer US rate expectations. Analysts told CNBC-TV18 a weaker rupee cushioned domestic prices while physical demand stayed steady but cautious.

items.title: Mounting rate hike bets keep weekly loss in sight for gold
items.summary: Spot gold slipped 0.1% to $4,274.94 an ounce on Friday and headed for a weekly loss of about 2.4% as sticky inflation, hawkish Fed signals and higher Treasury yields dented bullion's appeal, Reuters reported. Traders priced a 64% chance of an October rate hike and 93% for December, with bullion sitting about 19% below its February 27 peak.

items.title: Gold falls 5th week running as AI tech spending surges
items.summary: London gold fell 1.8% week-on-week to about $4,268, its fifth straight weekly decline, while silver dropped 5.3% to below $63.50 as heavy AI-related corporate borrowing pushed the US 10-year Treasury yield above 5.20%, BullionVault reported. The selloff came despite persistent geopolitical risk around the Strait of Hormuz.

items.title: Gold price outlook: MCX gold slips for the week as US Fed rate hike bets rise
items.summary: MCX October gold fell about ₹3,500 per 10 grams on the week to ₹1,50,891, erasing September's gains as hawkish Fed signals and a 19-year high in the US 10-year yield weighed on bullion, Mint reported. Fed Governor Michael Barr said further rate hikes 'are likely to be needed' to return inflation to 2%.

items.title: Wall Street split on gold's path after drop below $4,300; Main Street stays bullish
items.summary: The Kitco News weekly gold survey showed Wall Street evenly split — 36% bullish, 29% bearish, 36% neutral — after spot gold broke below $4,300 and set a weekly low of $4,244.63. Main Street kept its bullish majority, with 57% of 152 retail voters expecting gains as a heavy US jobs-data week looms.

items.title: Gold's $4,300 support faces another test as bond yields surge and jobs data looms
items.summary: Analysts told Kitco News that gold's resilience above $4,300 is being tested by 10-year yields at a two-decade high of 5.20%, with Saxo Bank's Ole Hansen watching $4,235 as the next support. A softer-than-expected US jobs report could pull yields and the dollar lower and unlock upside, while a hot print would reinforce pressure.

items.title: Kotak sees downside risk to FY27 gold import forecast as imports slide
items.summary: Kotak Institutional Equities sees downside risk to its $88 billion FY27 gold import forecast after India imported just $17.5 billion in the first five months of the fiscal year. Kotak attributed the weakness partly to the May 13 import-duty increase from 6% to 15% and elevated domestic prices denting physical demand.

items.title: India's forex reserves fall $14.88 billion to $765.90 billion: RBI
items.summary: India's foreign exchange reserves fell $14.88 billion to $765.90 billion in the week ended September 18, RBI data showed, driven by a $14.82 billion drop in foreign currency assets. Gold reserves rose $68 million to $111.29 billion, marginally offsetting the decline.

items.title: Gold may rise to $5,000/oz in H1 2027 after near-term consolidation, says ICICI Bank
items.summary: ICICI Bank expects gold to consolidate in the near term before climbing to $5,000 an ounce in the first half of 2027, supported by central-bank buying and investment demand. The bank's analysts see domestic prices trading in a ₹1.40 lakh to ₹1.60 lakh range through the rest of 2026 as festive and wedding demand offers support.

items.title: Gold hits low of $4,254 after final consumer sentiment rises to 48.1
items.summary: Spot gold dropped to $4,254 an ounce after the University of Michigan's final September consumer sentiment reading came in at 48.1, above expectations, while year-ahead inflation expectations jumped to 4.6%, the highest since June. The data reinforced bets that the Fed will keep rates higher for longer.

items.title: Augmont Enterprises empanelled by NSE to promote Electronic Gold Receipts
items.summary: The National Stock Exchange has empanelled Augmont Enterprises to promote Electronic Gold Receipts, the exchange-traded instrument backed by physical gold held in vaults. The move aims to deepen participation in paper gold as Indian investors shift from physical holdings to regulated electronic formats.
